messages.subject: Getting variables into ggplot environment
parts:
Hi all,

I am having trouble getting percent on the y-axis of a ggplot stacked histogram from a grouped dataframe. Normally, `y = (..count..)/sum(..count..)`
accomplishes this, but with the grouped dataframe, `sum(..count..)` seems to be summing the ungrouped entries. Note the y-axis:

require(ggplot)
require(dplyr)
set.seed(95616)
df <- data.frame(group1=rep(letters[1:10], each=5),
                 question=rep(1:5),
                 answer=sample(1:4, 50, replace=T))

df %>%
  group_by(group1, question) %>%
  summarise(response = median(answer)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = question,
             y = (..count..)/sum(..count..),
             fill=as.factor(response))) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())

To get the proper percentages, I need to divide the counts by the number of groups, which is `nlevels(df$group1)`, 10. Using `y = (..count..)/10` works, but I want to do it programmatically and can't. I've tried a bunch of ways (below) to bring `nlevels(df$group1)` into the y aes expression, and all fail. Any ideas?


df %>%
  group_by(group1, question) %>%
  summarise(response = median(answer)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = question,
             y = (..count..)/nlevels(group1),
             fill=as.factor(response))) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())

df <- cbind(df, n.levels=nlevels(df$group1))
df %>%
  group_by(group1, question) %>%
  summarise(response = median(answer)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = question,
             y = (..count..)/n.levels[1],
             fill=as.factor(response))) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())

n.levels <- nlevels(df$group1)
.e <- environment()
df %>%
  group_by(group1, question) %>%
  summarise(response = median(answer)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = question,
             y = (..count..)/n.levels,
             fill=as.factor(response)),
         environment = .e) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())

n.levels <- nlevels(df$group1)
df %>%
  group_by(group1, question) %>%
  summarise(response = median(answer)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = question,
             y = (..count..)/n.levels,
             fill=as.factor(response)),
         environment = environment()) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Getting variables into ggplot environment
parts:
Since no one has replied yet, I took a look at this.  Perhaps this is what you need:

require(ggplot2)
require(scales)

df %.%
   group_by(group1, question) %.%
   summarise(response = median(answer)) %.%
   ggplot(aes(x = question, 
              fill=as.factor(response))) +
   geom_bar(position="fill") +
   scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())


Bonnie
